validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: strongly confirmed, real Soviet-era transcontinental trunk gas pipeline, not a GEM-only entity. Independent corroboration from six separate origins: (1) the Great Soviet Encyclopedia's 'Магистральный газопровод' entry (booksite.ru, one of the sheet's own cited wiki sources) names 'двухниточная система Бухара — Урал' among the USSR's largest gas transport systems and gives 'Первая очередь Г. Бухара — Урал протяжённостью 2200 км, диаметром 1020 мм' -- an EXACT match to this row's own Length/Diameter and SegmentName='I' ('первая очередь' = first stage/line); (2) АО «Гипроспецгаз» (the actual Soviet design institute that engineered the line) publishes a detailed corporate history (gsg.spb.ru) confirming construction 1961-1966, route from Gazli through Kyzylkum/Karakum/Ustyurt to the Urals, 1020mm domestic pipe, 17 compressor + 22 gas-distribution stations; (3) uglevodorody.ru's pipeline database entry (owner=Gazprom, length 4,537 km, 'состояние: в эксплуатации' / status: operating, notes a fall-2014 reverse-flow mode); (4) ru.wikipedia.org corroborates length >4,500 km, 1020mm pipe, 17+22 stations, and names Chelyabinsk explicitly among the 33 Ural cities supplied; (5) intergas.kz's official 'About the company' page lists 'МГ «Бухара-Урал»' as one of the trunk lines actively managed today under BOTH UMG Aktobe and UMG Kostanai divisions (consistent with two parallel strings running through different Kazakh regions en route to different Russian oblasts); (6) two 2023 Kazakh/Uzbek news outlets (gazeta.uz, aktobetimes.kz) describe the EXISTING two lines as overloaded ('загружены на 170%' last winter) and under active government attention for a third feeder branch -- unambiguous evidence the pipeline is operating today, not idle or phantom. OSM/geometry (Tier 3, location-only): the OSM reconciliation run found an unnamed 614.7 km trace along this row's own drawn route corridor (disposition FRAGMENT_OF_EXISTING, route IoU 0.246 against GEM's already-'high'-accuracy route) -- independent satellite-derived geometry sits on top of the claimed corridor, consistent with existence. CLASSIFICATION: correct. Every source treats this as a 'магистральный газопровод' (trunk/transmission gas pipeline), never a gathering or feeder line -- Fuel=Gas and PipelineType=transmission are both well supported. DUPLICATE: checked against the roster's other 'Bukhara-Ural' row, P5695 (2,382 km, Gazli->Sverdlovsk Oblast, same Capacity=21.0, same Diameter='1000, 1020'). This is NOT a bibliographic duplicate/double-count -- Bukhara-Ural genuinely was built and is operated as TWO PARALLEL PHYSICAL STRINGS. The Giprospetsgaz institute's own account and multiple press pieces describe construction reaching Chelyabinsk first, then continuing on to Sverdlovsk/Nizhny Tagil -- i.e. an extension pattern consistent with GEM's two rows having different Russian-oblast endpoints (Chelyabinsk vs Sverdlovsk) off the same Gazli origin. BSE's 'первая очередь = 2,200 km' is an EXACT match for THIS row (P2289); summing P2289 (2,200) + P5695 (2,382) = 4,582 km, which sits within ~1-2% of the three independent whole-system totals found (BSE 4,503 km; Giprospetsgaz 4,464 km 'в однониточном исполнении'; uglevodorody.ru 4,537 km) -- strong circumstantial confirmation that P2289 and P5695 are the system's two real, distinct strings, not one pipe recorded twice. No merge recommended. Note for the record: intergas.kz's operating-division list (UMG Aktobe carries 'МГ «Бухара-Урал»' while UMG Kostanai separately also carries 'МГ «Бухара-Урал»') is consistent with, though does not on its own prove, a two-string reading.

validity.recommendation: Capacity=21.00 bcm/y is very likely the two-line SYSTEM's combined/design-era total, mis-stamped identically onto BOTH per-string rows (P2289 AND P5695 both carry 21.0) -- the same 'one system number on multiple strings' defect pattern flagged elsewhere in this pass. Do not treat as resolved; needs a genuine per-string figure or an explicit note that both rows intentionally share the system total. Separately, StartYear1=1963 is not cleanly corroborated -- the most authoritative source found (the pipeline's own design institute) points to gas reaching Chelyabinsk in 1964 and full two-line system commissioning in 1966, not 1963. Recommend re-checking against a source that states 1963 verbatim for the Gazli-Chelyabinsk leg specifically before treating it as confirmed.
validity.researcher_notes: CAPACITY (GEM: 21.00 bcm/y, identical on both P2289 and P5695): the number 21 IS independently attested, but every source that gives it frames it as the TWO-LINE SYSTEM total, never a single string's own throughput. The Great Soviet Encyclopedia entry (booksite.ru) states explicitly: 'двухниточная система Бухара — Урал ... пропускной способностью 21 млрд. м3 в год' -- 21 bcm/y for the whole two-line system as originally designed, immediately followed in the same sentence by the SAME source giving the Central Asia-Center two-line system's capacity as 25 bcm/y (a different pipeline family that shows the identical per-system-not-per-string framing). If GEM's two rows are each individually carrying the system's 21 bcm/y figure, the implied combined total (42 bcm/y) is roughly double any other figure found: the RPI 2009 industry report ('Oil and Gas Industry of Turkmenistan', s3.amazonaws.com/rgi-documents PDF -- note: fails url_verifier's automated content screen because the PDF is 3+ MB, a documented large-PDF false-negative; manually confirmed via `pdftotext -layout`, 'Bukhara-Urals'/'Bukhara-Ural' appear on lines 2172/3234/3243/3315) states the Bukhara-Ural TWO-LINE system's DESIGN capacity is 15 bcm/y, with actual current throughput only 3.5 bcm/y (Uzbek section) to 7.5 bcm/y (Russian section). KMG's own Annual Report table (ar2019.kmg.kz / ar2020.kmg.kz, EN PDFs -- same large-PDF false-negative on the automated screen, manually confirmed via pdftotext: 'Bukhara-Ural 2,382 44.6' [sic, actually 31.5 per the layout-preserved column] at line ~137/93) lists 'Bukhara-Ural' as a single table row at 2,382 km / 31.5 bcm/y -- notably, that LENGTH is an exact match for P5695, not P2289, yet KMG presents it as ONE row, reinforcing that KMG's own accounting does not cleanly split the system into two per-string figures either. Most tellingly, TWO independent 2023 sources describing the pipeline's actual current operation put the real combined throughput far lower still: ru.wikipedia.org states 'Пропускная мощность - 8 млрд. куб. м газа в год' (8 bcm/y) and gazeta.uz quotes an industry source giving the same figure ('«Бухара — Урал» — около 8 млрд кубометров'). So across five independent reference points the SYSTEM-level capacity ranges from 8 (current actual, 2023) to 15 (design, 2009) to 21 (design, Soviet-era BSE) to 31.5/44.6 (KMG AR2019-21, two different vintages of the same publisher, so really one origin) -- and NONE of them supports 21.0 bcm/y as this ONE STRING's own throughput. Recommend leaving Capacity unresolved/flagged rather than treating the existing 21.00 value as sourced. STARTYEAR1 (GEM: 1963): could not independently confirm. Giprospetsgaz's own institutional history (the design institute, arguably the single most authoritative source available) quotes a contemporaneous Chelyabinskiy Rabochiy newspaper article from NOVEMBER 1964 describing the first-stage construction as having just 'Дошли до Челябинска и двинулись к Свердловску' (reached Chelyabinsk and moved on toward Sverdlovsk) -- i.e. as of Nov 1964 the line was only just reaching Chelyabinsk, not already operating there since 1963. The same source states the pipeline (both lines together) was formally 'сдан в эксплуатацию' (commissioned) in 1966. Separately, Sverdlovsk (the endpoint of the OTHER string, P5695) got its first gas 1 December 1964 per both agenda-u.org and a search-summarized Yekaterinburg city-portal piece (ekburg.ru, page fetch failed/unreachable from this environment so not independently re-verified) -- and Chelyabinsk demonstrably received gas BEFORE that Dec-1964 Sverdlovsk date (agenda-u.org: '...Челябинским трубопрокатным заводами в 1964 году голубой факел запылал в Свердловске...' -- Chelyabinsk plants named as having already been supplied by the time Sverdlovsk lit up in 1964). Putting these together, the best-supported reading is that Chelyabinsk received first gas sometime in 1964 (not 1963), with full two-line system completion in 1966. This is only a one-year gap from GEM's 1963, and I did find one general-purpose web search summary asserting 'Первая нитка ... Газли-Челябинск ... запущена в 1963 году' -- but I could not trace that claim to a specific page I directly fetched and verified, so I am not citing it as a ref (standing rule 2: no fabricated/unverified sourcing). Net: StartYear1=1963 is plausible and only mildly in tension with the evidence, but not cleanly confirmed by the strongest available primary account.

summary: P2289 (Bukhara-Ural Gas Pipeline, Line I, Gazli->Chelyabinsk): existence, classification, and duplicate status all CONFIRMED -- six independent RU sources (incl. the pipeline's own Soviet design institute Giprospetsgaz) corroborate a real, actively-operated two-string trunk system, with BSE's 'первая очередь = 2,200 km/1020mm' an exact match for this row and P5695 confirmed as the genuine second parallel string, not a duplicate. Length (2,200 km) and FuelSource/Location (Gazli->Chelyabinsk) refs added at medium/high tier. TWO spec concerns staged: Capacity=21.00 bcm/y is very likely the two-line SYSTEM's design-era total mis-stamped identically on both P2289 and P5695 (five independent sources give five different system-level figures -- 8/15/21/31.5/44.6 bcm/y -- none matching 21 as a per-string number); and StartYear1=1963 is only weakly supported, with the most authoritative source (the design institute itself) pointing to 1964 (Chelyabinsk) / 1966 (full system commissioning) instead. Both left UNRESOLVED rather than force a ref. Diameter's '1000' component (of '1000, 1020') is also unconfirmed (1020 alone is solid) -- left UNRESOLVED.
